jobs.description:
Description

This position is part of the Timberlands Science & Technology (S&T) organization and reports to the Remote Sensing Manager, part of the Advanced Forestry Systems platform.

The LiDAR/UAV Scientist at Weyerhaeuser is a member of the Remote Sensing team and partly responsible for the acquisition, processing, and analysis of airborne and close-range remote sensing data to support Timberlands business decisions. Supporting the acquisition of aerial LiDAR data for internal inventory programs is a core responsibility for the role. This role requires expertise in LiDAR, UAV operations, and digital photogrammetry, along with proficiency in remote sensing and geospatial technologies.

This is a hybrid in-office position (work in the office Tuesday-Thursday). The preferred location for this role is Centralia, WA. Will also consider candidates to work from Hot Springs (AR), New Bern (NC), Springfield (OR), Vancouver (WA).

Essential Job Functions:

Participate in acquisition and management of LiDAR, aerial imagery, and UAS data in collaboration with Technology and Timberlands teams.
Generate, process, and maintain remote sensing datasets and LiDAR-derived products with rigorous quality control.
Design and enhance decision support tools integrating multi-temporal and multi-spectral remotely sensed data (from active and passive sensors).
Apply remote sensing principles and develop analytical techniques to solve operational problems and improve data applications.
Develop advanced image and signal processing code for feature extraction, classification, and machine learning algorithms.
Support training, and expert input on UAS systems, LiDAR data, and remote sensing strategies.
Prepare and review technical reports, present findings, and support strategic planning with the RS unit manager and stakeholders.
Conduct scientific analyses by correlating remote sensing data with ground truth and modeled results, supporting company objectives through modeling and documentation.
Participate in the development of strategies related to LiDAR, UAV and Terrestrial sensor technology and data collection.
Field work and business travel are required. Driving safety vehicles in forest roads is considered.

Qualifications

Education and Experience Requirements:

MSc or PhD degree with 1+ years of experience in applied sciences such as forestry, Geomatics, natural resources, with a strong emphasis in GIS or Remote Sensing.
Experience in traditional machine learning, deep learning, and computer vision.
UAV experience in data collection is a plus.
Part 107 UAV license available or willing to obtain.
Knowledge and experience in the application of the principles of remote sensors, field checking and image processing, and interpretation of forest or natural resource management.
Experience in programming (Python, R), directly through a computer science degree program or from ancillary coursework to support another degree or professional activity.
Competency in the use of statistical tools (e.g., R), and an understanding of spatial statistics.
Proficient in remote sensing-GIS tools: ArcGIS, QT Modeler, QGIS. Other Skills and Attributes
Strong communication and interpersonal skills are essential.
Demonstrated ability to work on projects collaboratively as part of a team.

About Weyerhaeuser
We sustainably manage forests and manufacture products that make the world a better place. We’re serious about safety, driven to achieve excellence, and proud of what we do. With multiple business lines in locations across North America, we offer a range of exciting career opportunities for smart, talented people who are passionate about making a difference.
We know you have a choice in your career. We want you to choose us.

Find out more about Weyerhaeuser at www.weyerhaeuser.com and learn our Story here: https://youtu.be/c2R_lQ7wo0A

We believe trees are a remarkable resource that can and should be managed responsibly to make a range of products that meet human needs, while also providing recreation, wildlife habitat, and other important ecosystem benefits.
For more than a century, we've been taking care of forests to make life better.

What We Offer...
Compensation: This role is eligible for our annual merit-increase program, and we are targeting a salary range of $90,244 - $135,509 based on your level of skills, qualifications and experience. You will also be eligible for our Annual Incentive Program, which offers a cash bonus targeting 7% of base pay. Potential plan funding may range from zero to two times that target.

We offer a pre-tax Health Savings Account option which includes a company contribution. Other benefit options are also available such as voluntary Long-Term Care and Employee Assistance Programs. Summary

The Getty Post-Baccalaureate Conservation Internships aim to increase the number of students from underrepresented backgrounds preparing to enroll in graduate degree programs related to museum conservation.

An advanced degree is essential to a conservation career and few programs exist. Applicants often boost their credentials by completing prerequisite courses and undertaking up to thousands of hours of conservation training, usually unpaid. Graduate program administrators say these realities have limited opportunities for underrepresented groups.

Launched in 2020 as a pilot program, the Getty Post-Baccalaureate Internships are the first nationwide effort to provide yearlong financial support and hands-on conservation experience to underrepresented post-baccalaureates who are preparing to apply to conservation graduate programs.

Program Structure

Based on departmental needs, interns will be placed at conservation studios and labs at the Getty Center and Getty Villa in Los Angeles for the first six months of their internships, and then at a Los Angeles-area museum or within a different conservation department at Getty for the second six months of the internship. Areas of focus for the internship may include American Indian collections and artifacts, conservation science, antiquities, sculpture and decorative arts, works on paper, photographs, or books.

For the second six months of the internship, placements have been previously offered at the Academy Museum of Motion Pictures; the Huntington; the Fowler Museum at UCLA; the Los Angeles County Museum of Art (LACMA); and the Autry Museum of the American West.

About Action For Humanity

Action For Humanity (AFH) is an international humanitarian and development organization working with communities affected by crisis and poverty. In Yemen, AFH delivers humanitarian, recovery and development programming across sectors including livelihoods and economic recovery, health, WASH, food security, protection, education and other community-based interventions. AFH works with government institutions, universities, donors, civil society, the private sector and communities to deliver accountable, sustainable and locally relevant solutions.

Project and Role Background

The project is an Islamic Development Bank-funded green business incubator and entrepreneurship initiative to be established in Hadramout University with key local stakeholders. The project will combine a practical, environmentally responsible incubation facility with business-development services for youth, women, entrepreneurs, start-ups and micro and small enterprises.

The Project Manager will lead the project from technical preparation and construction/fit-out through operationalization and program delivery, ensuring the facility is safe, adaptable, cost-conscious, environmentally responsible and appropriate to the Yemeni context. The Project Manager is the senior focal point responsible for overall planning, technical leadership, delivery, quality, compliance and results. The role requires a strong engineer and manager who can connect civil works and green design with procurement, stakeholder coordination and the operational needs of a business incubator.

Key Responsibilities

Project Leadership and Delivery

Lead day-to-day implementation against approved scope, budget, schedule, results and donor requirements.
Maintain the implementation plan, milestone schedule, procurement plan, cash forecast, risk register and action tracker.
Coordinate Programs, Engineering, Operations, Procurement, Finance, MEAL and partners, and resolve implementation bottlenecks promptly.

Civil Engineering, Design and Construction

Lead and coordinate site assessments, design reviews, drawings, technical specifications, BOQs and construction schedules.
Ensure designs are durable, functional and adapted to Hadramout/Yemen, including heat, energy reliability, water efficiency, local materials, accessibility and maintenance costs.
Oversee construction, rehabilitation, fit-out and installation; monitor workmanship, materials, quantities, progress, variations and defects.
Coordinate inspections, testing, commissioning, handover, warranties, as-built documentation and defect follow-up.

Green Building and Environmental Management

Integrate practical green-building measures such as passive cooling/shading, energy and water efficiency, renewable-energy options, waste reduction, responsible materials and lifecycle-cost considerations.
Identify and manage environmental, social, health and safety risks during construction and operation.
Prioritize climate-resilient and locally maintainable solutions suitable for the Yemeni context.

Incubator Operational Readiness

Lead the transition from construction to a functioning incubator, including furniture, equipment, ICT, utilities, safety systems, maintenance plans and operating procedures.
Ensure the space supports training, co-working, mentoring, innovation, administration and inclusive access.
Work with enterprise-development colleagues to align the facility with incubation, mentoring, market-linkage and access-to-finance activities.

Procurement, Budget and Contract Oversight

Provide technical input to tender packages, specifications, bid evaluations, contractor/consultant selection and procurement tracking in line with AFH procedures.
Monitor expenditure, commitments, forecasts and variations; support value for money and disciplined change control.
Verify technical completion and quality before recommending certification/payment, subject to required independent checks and approvals.

Stakeholder and Donor Coordination

Coordinate with relevant donor representatives, Hadramout University, government counterparts, technical authorities, contractors, private-sector actors and other stakeholders.
Prepare technical meetings, field visits, presentations, action trackers and decision records, and represent the project when delegated.

MEAL, Reporting and Team Management

Work with MEAL to establish indicators, monitoring tools and evidence for infrastructure and program results.
Prepare high-quality technical and narrative inputs for donor reports, management updates and project reviews.
Maintain complete project records, including designs, approvals, inspection records, variations, progress evidence and handover files.
Supervise assigned staff and consultants and establish clear responsibilities, deadlines and performance follow-up.

Risk, Compliance and Safeguarding

Maintain an active risk register covering construction, environmental, safety, financial, procurement, schedule, stakeholder and operational risks.
Ensure compliance with AFH policies, applicable donor requirements, relevant Yemeni regulations, approved technical standards and contractual obligations.
Apply safeguarding, PSEA, anti-fraud, anti-corruption, conflict-of-interest and accountability requirements throughout implementation.

Education

Essential: Bachelor’s degree in Civil Engineering, Environmental Engineering with strong civil/infrastructure background, or a closely related engineering field.
Preferred: Master’s degree in Civil/Environmental Engineering, Construction or Project Management, Sustainable/Green Building, Environmental Management or a related discipline.
Relevant professional certification in project management, green building, construction management, HSE or contract management is an advantage.

Experience

Minimum 7 years of progressively responsible experience in civil/infrastructure, construction or engineering project management, including at least 3 years in a project leadership or senior coordination role.
Demonstrated experience delivering buildings, institutional facilities, training centers, incubators, innovation/enterprise spaces or comparable multi-use facilities.
Strong experience in design review, BOQs/specifications, tendering, contractor management, site supervision, quality control, variations, commissioning and handover.

Experience with incubators, innovation hubs, training centers, university facilities, green buildings or flexible multi-use spaces should be highlighted where available.

Understanding of green construction, passive design, energy/water efficiency, climate resilience and lifecycle costing.
Strong project planning, budget control, procurement, contract administration and risk-management skills.

jobs.description:
Overview

If you’re ready for more than a job, Trutech Wildlife Service offers a career with purpose.

Are you looking for a hands-on career, not just a job? Do you have experience in construction, roofing, insulation, or home improvement and want to put those skills to work in a stable, recession-resistant industry?

Trutech Wildlife Service specializes in wildlife management services for residential and commercial properties, providing humane wildlife removal, exclusion, and damage repair solutions nationwide. We help customers resolve wildlife-related concerns in safe, effective, and environmentally responsible ways while protecting homes, businesses, and communities.

This role is ideal for individuals with a background in construction, repair, or related trades who are committed to craftsmanship and accountability. You’ll play a critical role in preventing future wildlife intrusions by performing exclusion work, repairs, and remediation while maintaining high safety and quality standards.

Trutech Wildlife Service is a brand that invests in its people. If you are a driven professional who embraces our values and upholds our standards of excellence, you’ll find opportunities to succeed, grow, and advance within our organization.

Responsibilities

As a Wildlife Exclusion/Repair Service Technician
at Trutech Wildlife Service, you perform hands-on exclusion, repair, and remediation services for residential and commercial properties. You identify entry points, complete structural repairs, and implement humane wildlife prevention solutions while following safety, technical, and quality guidelines.

What Does a Day in the Life Look Like?

Perform interior and exterior property inspections, including roofs, attics, crawlspaces, and other confined spaces, to identify wildlife entry points and potential vulnerabilities.
Install preventative exclusion materials such as screens, chimney caps, vent covers, and other barriers to prevent wildlife access.
Complete minor repairs to roofs, siding, foundations, and other structural areas where wildlife may gain entry.
Safely remove wildlife using humane trapping and relocation techniques in accordance with company standards and regulations.
Maintain accurate documentation of services performed, materials used, and customer interactions.
Provide clear, detailed reports and review completed scopes of work with customers.
Collaborate with sales and customer service teams to ensure seamless and positive customer experience.
Follow up with customers to confirm satisfaction and address any additional concerns or recommendations.

What type of benefits will you receive?

Competitive hourly range: $20 - $20
Comprehensive benefits package including health, dental, and vision insurance.
401k with generous match, Employee Stock Purchase Plan (ESPP).
6 Paid Holidays Annually!
PTO accrual based on tenure - 3 weeks beginning first full year!
Tuition reimbursement up to $5,250/year (federal max!) OR free tuition on approved programs through Purdue Global!!!
Ongoing training and professional development opportunities!
Supportive team environment with a focus on work-life balance.
Opportunities for career advancement within the Rollins Family of Brands!

Qualifications

What do you need to be successful?

High school diploma or equivalent; college degree is a plus
Valid driver’s license
Proven experience in construction, carpentry, roofing, or other related fields
Ability to work in the field independently
Strong problem-solving skills and attention to detail
Proficiency in using several types of software and applications

What does the work environment look like?

We go where the wildlife goes! Candidates must be physically capable of safely performing the following job duties with or without reasonable accommodation.

Must be able to drive to various locations, often covering large territories.
Frequent walking, standing, and moving through diverse types of terrain, including uneven ground, stairs, roofs, and sometimes slippery or muddy areas.
Ability to work outdoors in various weather conditions (extreme heat, extreme cold, rain, snow, etc.).
Must have the ability to climb stairs and ladders safely.
Must be able to crouch, kneel, bend, and stretch frequently.
Capability to carry and use equipment necessary for inspections and minor control measures (Traps, ladders, inspection tools, etc).
Ability to lift and carry up to 50 pounds regularly.
Clear verbal communication skills to interact effectively with clients and team members.

Join us in making a positive impact on nuisance wildlife management and become a part of our dedicated team today!

Summary

The Getty Post-Baccalaureate Conservation Internships aim to increase the number of students from underrepresented backgrounds preparing to enroll in graduate degree programs related to museum conservation.

An advanced degree is essential to a conservation career and few programs exist. Applicants often boost their credentials by completing prerequisite courses and undertaking up to thousands of hours of conservation training, usually unpaid. Graduate program administrators say these realities have limited opportunities for underrepresented groups.

Launched in 2020 as a pilot program, the Getty Post-Baccalaureate Internships are the first nationwide effort to provide yearlong financial support and hands-on conservation experience to underrepresented post-baccalaureates who are preparing to apply to conservation graduate programs.

Program Structure

Based on departmental needs, interns will be placed at conservation studios and labs at the Getty Center and Getty Villa in Los Angeles for the first six months of their internships, and then at a Los Angeles-area museum or within a different conservation department at Getty for the second six months of the internship. Areas of focus for the internship may include American Indian collections and artifacts, conservation science, antiquities, sculpture and decorative arts, works on paper, photographs, or books.

For the second six months of the internship, placements have been previously offered at the Academy Museum of Motion Pictures; the Huntington; the Fowler Museum at UCLA; the Los Angeles County Museum of Art (LACMA); and the Autry Museum of the American West.

new_jobs.description:
Overview

If you’re ready for more than a job, Trutech Wildlife Service offers a career with purpose.

Are you looking for a hands-on career, not just a job? Do you have experience in construction, roofing, insulation, or home improvement and want to put those skills to work in a stable, recession-resistant industry?

Trutech Wildlife Service specializes in wildlife management services for residential and commercial properties, providing humane wildlife removal, exclusion, and damage repair solutions nationwide. We help customers resolve wildlife-related concerns in safe, effective, and environmentally responsible ways while protecting homes, businesses, and communities.

This role is ideal for individuals with a background in construction, repair, or related trades who are committed to craftsmanship and accountability. You’ll play a critical role in preventing future wildlife intrusions by performing exclusion work, repairs, and remediation while maintaining high safety and quality standards.

Trutech Wildlife Service is a brand that invests in its people. If you are a driven professional who embraces our values and upholds our standards of excellence, you’ll find opportunities to succeed, grow, and advance within our organization.

Responsibilities

As a Wildlife Exclusion/Repair Service Technician
at Trutech Wildlife Service, you perform hands-on exclusion, repair, and remediation services for residential and commercial properties. You identify entry points, complete structural repairs, and implement humane wildlife prevention solutions while following safety, technical, and quality guidelines.

What Does a Day in the Life Look Like?

Perform interior and exterior property inspections, including roofs, attics, crawlspaces, and other confined spaces, to identify wildlife entry points and potential vulnerabilities.
Install preventative exclusion materials such as screens, chimney caps, vent covers, and other barriers to prevent wildlife access.
Complete minor repairs to roofs, siding, foundations, and other structural areas where wildlife may gain entry.
Safely remove wildlife using humane trapping and relocation techniques in accordance with company standards and regulations.
Maintain accurate documentation of services performed, materials used, and customer interactions.
Provide clear, detailed reports and review completed scopes of work with customers.
Collaborate with sales and customer service teams to ensure seamless and positive customer experience.
Follow up with customers to confirm satisfaction and address any additional concerns or recommendations.

What type of benefits will you receive?

Competitive hourly range: $20 - $20
Comprehensive benefits package including health, dental, and vision insurance.
401k with generous match, Employee Stock Purchase Plan (ESPP).
6 Paid Holidays Annually!
PTO accrual based on tenure - 3 weeks beginning first full year!
Tuition reimbursement up to $5,250/year (federal max!) OR free tuition on approved programs through Purdue Global!!!
Ongoing training and professional development opportunities!
Supportive team environment with a focus on work-life balance.
Opportunities for career advancement within the Rollins Family of Brands!

Qualifications

What do you need to be successful?

High school diploma or equivalent; college degree is a plus
Valid driver’s license
Proven experience in construction, carpentry, roofing, or other related fields
Ability to work in the field independently
Strong problem-solving skills and attention to detail
Proficiency in using several types of software and applications

What does the work environment look like?

We go where the wildlife goes! Candidates must be physically capable of safely performing the following job duties with or without reasonable accommodation.

Must be able to drive to various locations, often covering large territories.
Frequent walking, standing, and moving through diverse types of terrain, including uneven ground, stairs, roofs, and sometimes slippery or muddy areas.
Ability to work outdoors in various weather conditions (extreme heat, extreme cold, rain, snow, etc.).
Must have the ability to climb stairs and ladders safely.
Must be able to crouch, kneel, bend, and stretch frequently.
Capability to carry and use equipment necessary for inspections and minor control measures (Traps, ladders, inspection tools, etc).
Ability to lift and carry up to 50 pounds regularly.
Clear verbal communication skills to interact effectively with clients and team members.

Join us in making a positive impact on nuisance wildlife management and become a part of our dedicated team today!

new_jobs.description:
Senior Business Development Manager, Biomass Supply

Location
: Houston, TX. Remote-friendly, strong preference for Texas or the Southeast. Frequent travel to supplier sites and deployment regions

The Company

Our client is a Series A climate technology company converting agricultural and forestry waste into biochar through mobile pyrolysis. The resulting carbon removal credits are registry-certified and sold to major corporate buyers, and through 2026 the company is deploying systems across partner sites in North America.

The Role

This role owns the company's feedstock supply. You'll identify, pitch, and close partnerships with businesses that generate dry biomass residuals, turning their waste streams into long-term supply and host-site agreements as the business expands from one facility to multiple sites.
You'll focus on feedstock sources including nut shellers (pecan in particular), sawmills, wood products manufacturers, and other woody waste generators. The goal is to secure reliable, high-quality feedstock ahead of new deployments, build lasting supplier relationships, and identify the regions and residual streams best suited to the company's growth.

Key Responsibilities

Build and manage a pipeline of feedstock suppliers across agricultural and forestry markets
Identify and qualify supply sites based on volume, material quality, moisture content, and logistics
Structure and negotiate long-term B2B supply and site-hosting agreements
Secure feedstock ahead of new facility and unit deployments
Serve as the primary relationship owner for supply partners from first conversation through deployment
Work with operations to plan site layouts, deployment timelines, and material handling
Track residual volumes, pricing, and competing uses across target regions
Build the supply development process and, as the business scales, help develop a regional team

Background:

5–8 years of business development, procurement, or sourcing experience in agriculture, forestry, wood products, or waste-to-value
Existing network among nut processors, sawmills, wood fiber buyers, or similar residual generators
Proven track record of structuring and closing B2B commercial agreements
Strong understanding of biomass residual streams, including material specs, seasonality, and logistics
Credibility with plant managers, operators, and agricultural or forestry businesses
Ability to pitch a new or unfamiliar solution and develop supply from the ground up
Entrepreneurial mindset and comfort operating in an early-stage environment
Willingness to travel frequently to supplier sites, facilities, and deployment regions
Valid driver's license and authorization to work in the U.S. without sponsorship
